instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Take the pie crusts out of the fridge so they soften while you make the filling.
Chop the onion, peel and thinly slice the 2 carrots and slice the 8 oz mushrooms. Mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Pull the 3 cups cooked chicken into bite-size shreds. Leftover roast chicken or a store-bought rotisserie chicken both work. Chop 3 tbsp of the parsley.
Melt the 4 tbsp butter in a large pot over medium. Add the onion and carrots and cook for about 8 minutes, stirring now and then, until they're soft.
Add the mushrooms and cook for about 5 minutes, until they've let go of their liquid and started to brown. Add the garlic and stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell it.
Sprinkle the 1/4 cup flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for 2 minutes.
Pour in the 1 1/2 cups broth a little at a time, stirring as you go, then add the 1/3 cup cream. Bring it to a simmer and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until it's as thick as gravy.
Stir in the 1 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Taste it. It should be well seasoned, so add a pinch more salt if it's flat.
Stir in the chicken, the 3/4 cup frozen peas (no need to thaw them) and the chopped parsley. Take the pot off the heat and let it cool for 10 minutes.
Unroll one crust into a 9-inch pie plate and press it into the bottom and up the sides. Spoon in the filling and spread it level.

Lay the second crust over the top. Tuck the overhang of the top crust under the edge of the bottom crust and press them together all the way around with a fork or your fingers. Cut 4 or 5 short slits in the top.
Beat the egg in a small bowl and brush it over the top crust.

Set the pie on a rimmed baking sheet and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the filling is bubbling through the slits. If the edges brown too fast, cover them with strips of foil.
Let it rest for 15 minutes before you cut it. Any sooner and the filling runs out across the plate.
method_notes: Natasha's Kitchen leads: soften onion and carrots in butter, add mushrooms and garlic, cook flour into it, then stock and cream to a thick gravy before the chicken, frozen peas and parsley go in, all under a double crust baked at 425°F and rested 15 minutes. RecipeTin Eats poaches raw chicken in milk and broth and uses that liquid for the sauce, adds celery, wine and Parmesan, and tops individual pots with puff pastry at 350°F. This one cuts Natasha's deep-dish pie for 8 down to a standard 9-inch pie for 4, uses leftover cooked chicken and store-bought crusts in place of her homemade dough, and swaps her fine sea salt one for one with table salt.
